Oral; taken in divided doses per regimen (often after meals to reduce GI upset)
Caution and dose reduction in impairment (active 5-FU metabolite)
Avoid - additive GI and hepatic effects
CBC (myelosuppression), hand-foot syndrome, diarrhea/mucositis, liver function
summary: Doxifluridine (5'-deoxy-5-fluorouridine, 5'-DFUR) is an oral prodrug of 5-fluorouracil used as cytotoxic chemotherapy mainly for breast, colorectal, gastric and other solid tumors. It is NOT approved by the US FDA; it is marketed in parts of Asia (e.g., Japan, South Korea, China). It is converted to active 5-FU by the enzyme thymidine phosphorylase, which is present at higher concentrations in tumor tissue than in normal tissue, giving relatively tumor-selective activation. As a fluoropyrimidine it causes the expected class toxicities: myelosuppression, gastrointestinal effects (diarrhea, stomatitis/mucositis, nausea), and hand-foot syndrome (palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia), the latter being dose-limiting at high or prolonged exposures. Dosing follows the regional approved product and regimen (often several hundred milligrams to over 1 gram per day in divided doses). Because dosing, indications and full safety data are defined by non-FDA (regional) labeling rather than US labeling, prescribers should consult the applicable national product information.
indications: Per regional (non-US) labeling: treatment of certain solid tumors including breast cancer, colorectal cancer, gastric cancer, and other cancers (specific approved indications vary by country)
Note: NOT FDA-approved; indications are based on EMA/Asian regulatory product information and clinical literature

dosage.d: Dosing follows the applicable national product information; commonly in the range of about 800-1200 mg per day in divided doses, adjusted for tolerability and regimen
dosage.n: Exact dose/schedule per regional label and combination

dosage.d: Reduce dose or interrupt for significant myelosuppression, severe diarrhea/mucositis, or hand-foot syndrome

admin: Administer orally in divided doses per the regional protocol; taking with or after food may reduce gastrointestinal upset
Obtain baseline and periodic complete blood counts and assess GI and dermatologic toxicity before each cycle
Interrupt or reduce dose for severe diarrhea, stomatitis/mucositis, myelosuppression or hand-foot syndrome
Maintain adequate hydration and provide supportive care (antiemetics, antidiarrheals, skin care) as needed
Handle as a cytotoxic agent following standard precautions
moa: Doxifluridine is an oral prodrug of 5-fluorouracil. It is converted to 5-FU intracellularly by the enzyme thymidine phosphorylase (also called pyrimidine nucleoside phosphorylase), which is expressed at higher levels in many tumors than in normal tissues, conferring relative tumor selectivity. The resulting 5-FU is anabolized to fluorodeoxyuridine monophosphate (FdUMP), which inhibits thymidylate synthase and blocks DNA synthesis, and to fluorouridine triphosphate (FUTP), which is incorporated into RNA and disrupts RNA processing and function. These actions are cytotoxic to rapidly dividing cells.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to doxifluridine, 5-fluorouracil or fluoropyrimidines
relative: Pre-existing severe diarrhea, stomatitis, or active infection
Poor performance status or cardiac disease (fluoropyrimidine cardiotoxicity)

preg: Doxifluridine is a fluoropyrimidine cytotoxic agent and is contraindicated in pregnancy because of teratogenic and embryo-fetal toxicity. Females of reproductive potential should use effective contraception during treatment.
lact: Breastfeeding is contraindicated during treatment because of the potential for serious adverse effects in the infant from a cytotoxic fluoropyrimidine.
renal: Because the active metabolite 5-FU and its breakdown products are partly renally handled, use with caution and consider dose reduction in renal impairment; monitor for increased toxicity.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic impairment and monitor liver function; fluoropyrimidines can cause hepatotoxicity and impaired clearance may increase toxicity.

major: DPD inhibitors / sorivudine-type antivirals (brivudine, sorivudine) - markedly increase 5-FU toxicity; avoid
Other myelosuppressive chemotherapy or radiotherapy - additive myelotoxicity
Warfarin - fluoropyrimidines can potentiate anticoagulant effect (raised INR/bleeding)
moderate: Folinic acid (leucovorin) - enhances thymidylate synthase inhibition and toxicity (sometimes used intentionally)
Phenytoin - fluoropyrimidines may raise phenytoin levels
minor: Cimetidine and other agents may alter fluoropyrimidine metabolism
interactions.food: May be taken with food to reduce gastrointestinal upset per regional guidance.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol due to additive gastrointestinal irritation and hepatic stress.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor CBC, INR (if on warfarin), and liver/renal function tests during therapy.

serious: Myelosuppression (neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, anemia) with infection/bleeding risk
Cardiotoxicity (angina, arrhythmia - a fluoropyrimidine class effect)

monitoring: Complete blood count before each cycle and as clinically indicated
Gastrointestinal toxicity (diarrhea, stomatitis) at each visit
counsel: This is a chemotherapy tablet (a form of 5-fluorouracil); take it exactly as prescribed and do not change the dose on your own
Report severe diarrhea, mouth sores, fever or signs of infection, or unusual bruising/bleeding promptly
Tell your doctor about redness, peeling, tingling or pain in your palms and soles (hand-foot syndrome)
Use effective contraception during treatment; do not breastfeed; avoid alcohol
Keep all blood test and clinic appointments so your blood counts and organ function can be checked
pk: Cytotoxic effect develops over treatment cycles
Rapidly absorbed orally; converted to 5-FU with peak 5-FU levels within hours
Short - parent drug and 5-FU have short plasma half-lives (5-FU about 10-20 minutes)
Cyclical dosing maintains exposure across the treatment cycle
Store per the regional product label, typically at room temperature, protected from moisture
pearls: NOT FDA-approved - doxifluridine is an oral 5-FU prodrug marketed in parts of Asia (Japan/Korea/China); dosing and indications follow regional (non-US) product information and clinical literature
Activated to 5-FU by thymidine phosphorylase, which is enriched in tumor tissue, giving relative tumor selectivity
Fluoropyrimidine toxicities apply: myelosuppression, diarrhea, mucositis, and dose-limiting hand-foot syndrome
Screen for DPD deficiency risk; avoid brivudine/sorivudine; monitor INR if on warfarin
Contraindicated in pregnancy/lactation; handle and counsel as a cytotoxic agent
missed: If a dose is missed, follow the regional protocol; generally take it as soon as remembered unless it is close to the next scheduled dose, in which case skip it and resume the normal schedule - do not double the dose. Contact the oncology team if unsure or if multiple doses are missed.
overdose: Overdose produces exaggerated fluoropyrimidine toxicity: severe nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, mucositis, and especially severe and potentially life-threatening myelosuppression. There is no widely available specific antidote in routine practice (uridine triacetate is an antidote used for 5-fluorouracil/capecitabine overdose where available). Management is supportive: discontinue the drug, monitor and support blood counts (growth factors, transfusions), treat infection, and provide fluids and supportive care.
